raw_response:
The raw_customers table holds 230 rows for 200 distinct customers. 30 of them are historical rows with is_current=False and valid_from 2023-06-01, so they are SCD2 history. The join in silver_customers fans out those 30 customers, which explains 5415 vs 4699 (an extra 716 rows).

The fix is to keep only current rows in silver_customers. Each of the 200 customers has exactly one current row: is_current=True for 200 rows and 200 distinct customer_ids, and the 30 non-current rows are history for customers who also have a current row.

One check on the assumption: the 200 current rows with valid_from 2025-01-01 could in principle not be one per customer. But there are 200 distinct customers and 200 current rows, and all customers appear. If a customer had two current rows, another would have none, which is unlikely. The fix would be correct under that assumption.

A point-in-time join would be the alternative. Transactions run from 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-18, and every current row has valid_from 2025-01-01, so all transactions fall after it. The current row is therefore right for all of them.

The fix is to filter silver_customers on is_current. Output columns stay unchanged.
